headline: Three Bets, One Game, And A Thirteen Dollar Hole
paragraphs: Week 10 was less a slate than a rounding error. Five games graded, three waved off, two drew action, and three tickets went out at ten dollars apiece. One of them cashed. The final was 1-2 for a loss of 13.55 on thirty dollars staked, which works out to an ROI of negative 45.2 percent. Smallest week of the year, and it still found a way to be a bad one.

The entire story is Massachusetts 31, Ball State 30. The model took Massachusetts minus 3 at a 63 percent read and lost by a point of margin, then took Massachusetts on the moneyline at minus 155 with a 68 percent read and won 6.45. Best call and worst call, same field, same evening, separated by one point. The other play, Ohio minus 13.5 at 60 percent, died quietly in a 28-20 game. Spreads finished 0-2, moneylines 1-0.

Season to date across seven weeks graded for real: 162-202-10 on 374 plays, 44.5 percent winners against an expected 60.3, and 441.25 dollars gone from 3,740 staked for an ROI of negative 11.8 percent. There is also a hindsight week sitting off to the side at 40-25-1 and plus 110.47, which counts for exactly as much as a scorecard filled out after the bell. Of three plays whose line moved, one moved toward the model. That is 33.3 percent of nearly nothing.
